AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 1, 2021
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20, N-29-20, AND N-35-20, WHICH ALLOWS MEETINGS TO BE
VIDEOCONFERENCED WITHOUT PROVIDING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING, EITHER SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685
DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK ON AN ITEM. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32
OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-
agendas-393.
  5:00 PM
  VIDEOCONFERENCE
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a):
  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles
  County Sheriff representative, and other related City officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8056-016-139; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: Knights of Columbus; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  James C. Parker
  Executive Director of Regional Transportation

FLAG SALUTE
  Dennis Kato
  Interim Director of Public Safety

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS - None scheduled

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Senior Center Quarterly Drive-Through Birthday Celebration video.

  3.  Free Haircut and Backpack Giveaway event recap.

  4.  Memorial Day Tribute video.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.
 1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

2.  MEETING MINUTES - Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of May 18,
  2021. 825-04

  Minutes

3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period April 18, 2021 – May 1,
  2021, in the total amount of $908,810.26. 630

  Report

4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period May
  13 - May 26, 2021, in the total amount of $3,900,940.72. 640

  Warrant Register

5.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Ambrosio
  Decena, Heidi Decena, Jessica Decena, Elizabeth Valtierra, and Veronica Valtierra. 830-04/22

  Report

6.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS - MAY 26, 2021 - Receive and File report. 320

  Report

7.  RESOLUTION NO. 21-26 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS - Staff recommends City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 21-26, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE CITY CLERK AND
  SOCIAL SERVICES DEPARTMENTS. 870-02

  Report

8.  AUTHORIZATION  TO  EXECUTE  LANDSCAPE  MAINTENANCE AGREEMENTS  FOR
  LANDSCAPING ON HOXIE AVENUE AT THE 605 FREEWAY – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  approve a Landscape Maintenance agreement with the State of California, acting by and through
  the Department of Transportation;

  b.  approve a Landscape Maintenance agreement with McKenna Motors Norwalk, Inc. for the
  landscape maintenance area; and

  c.  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreements and any amendments, provided there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1025-01

  Report

9.  AGREEMENT FOR AUTO BODY REPAIR AND PAINTING SERVICES FOR SMALL-MEDIUM DUTY
  VEHICLES - Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with Wondries Family Collision
  Center for auto body repair and painting for small-medium duty vehicles for a three-year term from
  July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2024, with an option to extend the agreement for two one-year periods
  for a total contract value of $132,728; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement, and
  any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by
  the City Attorney. 634-05

  Report

10. RESOLUTION NO. 21-27 – APPROVING THE LETTER OF AGREEMENT BETWEEN CITY OF
  NORWALK AND INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF MACHINISTS AND AEROSPACE WORKERS,
  DISTRICT LODGE 947, LOCAL LODGE 1957 – NORWALK CITY EMPLOYEES ASSOCIATION –
  GENERAL AND HOURLY UNITS’ TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THE CURRENT COLLECTIVE
   BARGAINING AGREEMENT FOR A ONE YEAR PERIOD THROUGH JUNE 30, 2022 - Staff
  recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-27, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING THE LETTER OF AGREEMENT BETWEEN CITY OF
  NORWALK AND INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF MACHINISTS AND AEROSPACE WORKERS,
  DISTRICT LODGE 947, LOCAL LODGE 1957 – NORWALK CITY EMPLOYEES ASSOCIATION –
  GENERAL AND HOURLY UNITS’ TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THE CURRENT COLLECTIVE
  BARGAINING AGREEMENT FOR A ONE YEAR PERIOD THROUGH JUNE 30, 2022. 135-09

  Report

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 21-28 – APPROVING THE LETTER OF AGREEMENT BETWEEN CITY OF
  NORWALK AND THE NORWALK ASSOCIATION OF MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES FOR A ONE
  YEAR PERIOD THROUGH JUNE 30, 2022 - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-
  28, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING THE
  LETTER OF AGREEMENT BETWEEN CITY OF NORWALK AND THE NORWALK ASSOCIATION OF
  MANAGEMENT EMPLOYEES FOR A ONE YEAR PERIOD THROUGH JUNE 30, 2022. 135-17

  Report

  12. ORDINANCE NO. 21-1726 – APPROVING AN AMENDED AND RESTATED DEVELOPMENT
  AGREEMENT – MERCY HOUSING PROJECT - Staff recommends City Council introduce and waive
  first reading of Ordinance No. 21-1726, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING AN AMENDED AND RESTATED DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT WITH
  MERCY HOUSING CALIFORNIA RELATED TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE +/- 1.5 ACRE
  PROPERTY AT SAN ANTONIO DRIVE AND FOSTER ROAD; AND MAKING FINDINGS
  CONSISTENT WITH AND PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65867.5. 1405-01

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  13. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

REPORTS

  14. AGREEMENT - DIAL-A-RIDE PARATRANSIT USER SIDE SUBSIDY TRANSPORTATION PROGRAM
  – Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with Fiesta Taxi Cooperative, Inc. to provide
  Paratransit User Side Subsidy Transportation services for a three-year term from July 1, 2021 through
  June 30, 2024, with an option to extend the agreement for two one-year periods for a total contract
  value of $188,151; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments
  provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.
  1120-07

  Report

  15. ADOPTION OF 2021-2026 CITYWIDE PAVEMENT MANAGEMENT PROGRAM UPDATE,
  ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 21-15 – Staff recommends City Council adopt the 2021-2026 Update of
  the City-wide Pavement Management System for the Pavement Management Program. 1045-04

  Report

  16. CONSIDERATION OF A CITY SPEED HUMP POLICY - Staff recommends that City Council consider
  the information and provide direction towards development of a draft City speed hump policy that
  includes a detailed cost analysis for a speed hump program. 1050-09

  Report

  17. “THE WALK” - PROJECT UPDATE - Staff recommends City Council receive and file this report. 1405-
  04

  Report
   18. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – JUNE EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE – Receive and
  file. 710-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated May 27, 2021.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
